summary: Global reskinning uses CSS custom properties. Import doodleui-react/styles.css once, override variables on :root or a scoped wrapper, and optionally use DoodleUIProvider for React-level defaults.
precedence: Per-component prop (roughness, strokeWidth, bowing, sketchColor, fillStyle)
DoodleUIProvider prop (also sets scoped CSS vars)
CSS custom property on an ancestor

variables.name: --doodle-ui-roughness
variables.purpose: rough.js sketchiness intensity — higher looks messier

variables.name: --doodle-ui-fill-style
variables.purpose: Fill pattern when shapes have fill (hachure, solid, zigzag, cross-hatch, dots, dashed, zigzag-line)

variables.name: --doodle-ui-font-family
variables.purpose: Handwriting font stack — library does not load Google Fonts; set this after adding a font yourself

variables.name: --doodle-ui-color-error
variables.purpose: Error status color (also used for invalid form strokes)

darkMode.automatic: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) updates tokens when light is not forced
darkMode.explicit: data-theme="dark" or class "dark" on html or any ancestor
darkMode.forceLight: data-theme="light" or class "light" (wins over the media query)
darkMode.reactSubtree: <DoodleUIProvider theme="dark|light|system"> sets data-theme and palette for descendants

contrastNotes: WCAG AA requires ≥4.5:1 for normal text and ≥3:1 for non-text strokes
Thin hand-drawn strokes can look lighter than solid borders — test custom stroke-width and pastel inks
